title: Accessibility of right adjoints between presentable infinity categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be presentable infinity categories and let $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a coherent functor admitting a left adjoint, that is, a coherent functor $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ with coherent adjunction data $L\dashv R$ in the sense of [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]. Then there is an infinite regular cardinal $\rho\in\mathcal U$ such that $R$ preserves all small $\rho$-filtered colimits; that is, $R$ is accessible. The universes and coherent infinity-category notions used here are those of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data].

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.4.7.7 (a functor between accessible infinity categories admitting a left adjoint is accessible), used for the 'only if' direction of Corollary 5.5.2.9(2); Definition 5.5.3.1(3) and Proposition 5.5.3.3

proof.text: Choose an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ and an essentially small full subcategory $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal C$ of $\kappa$-compact objects which generates $\mathcal C$ under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. These are part of the accessibility assertion in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and presentability implies accessibility. Choose a small quasicategory $A$ and an equivalence $e:A\to\mathcal G$, as permitted by the definition of essentially small; write $g_a=e(a)$ for each vertex $a$ of $A$. Thus $(g_a)_{a\in A_0}$ is a small family and every object of $\mathcal G$ is equivalent to some $g_a$. Fix a left adjoint $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ of $R$ with coherent adjunction data $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\to RL$, $\epsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ as in [def-coef-coherent-adjunction-data]; its two triangle $2$-simplices are the triangle homotopies required in [lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence], which therefore gives the adjunct equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lc,d)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,Rd)$, $v\mapsto R(v)\circ\eta_c$, coherently natural in $c\in\mathcal C$ and $d\in\mathcal D$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7.7, proof: choose the small compact generating category and a left adjoint.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-common-compactness-rank] in the accessible category $\mathcal D$ to the small family $(L g_a)_{a\in A_0}$. It gives an infinite regular $\theta\in\mathcal U$ for which every $L g_a$ is $\theta$-compact. Put $\rho=\max(\kappa,\theta)$; as the maximum of two cardinals it is one of them, hence is infinite regular and belongs to $\mathcal U$. Any $\rho$-filtered quasicategory is both $\kappa$-filtered and $\theta$-filtered: every simplicial set with fewer than $\kappa$ or $\theta$ nondegenerate simplices also has fewer than $\rho$. Therefore each $g_a$ and each $L g_a$ is $\rho$-compact directly from the definition of compactness in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. The categories have all the colimits in question by presentability; no claim that accessibility ranks can be enlarged to an arbitrary regular cardinal is used.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7.7, proof: choose a common compactness rank for the images of the small family of generators.

proof.text:
Let $T:I\to\mathcal D$ be any coherent diagram with $I$ small and $\rho$-filtered. Choose colimiting cocones $t_i:T(i)\to y$ in $\mathcal D$ and $s_i:R T(i)\to z$ in $\mathcal C$, which exist by presentability. Applying $R$ to $t$ gives a cocone with vertex $Ry$, so the colimit property gives a comparison $q:z\to Ry$ with coherent identifications $q s_i\simeq R(t_i)$. For each $g=g_a$, compactness and the coherently natural adjunct equivalences of step 1 ([lem-coef-infinity-adjunction-mapping-equivalence], restricted along $T$ in the variable $d$) give equivalences in the common ambient category of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(g,z)\simeq\operatorname*{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(g,RT(i))\simeq\operatorname*{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lg,T(i))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lg,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(g,Ry).$$
The first and third equivalences are precisely preservation of this filtered colimiting cocone by the corresponding corepresentable functors, as defined in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Naturality of the adjunction identifies the map from its $i$th summand through the middle three terms with postcomposition by $R(t_i)$. Since $q s_i\simeq R(t_i)$, the displayed composite is postcomposition by $q$, including its coherent cocone data. Thus $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(g_a,q)$ is an equivalence for every $a$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7.7, proof, final paragraph: evaluation at a compact generator is the mapping-space functor corepresented by its left-adjoint image.

proof.text:
Precomposition by an equivalence in $\mathcal C$ is an equivalence on mapping spaces: its inverse is precomposition by an inverse edge, with inverse homotopies from associativity and units in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Consequently the conclusion of step 3 holds for every $g\in\mathcal G$, since such $g$ is equivalent to a $g_a$. For any $x\in\mathcal C$, choose a small $\kappa$-filtered presentation $P:J\to\mathcal G$ with colimit $x$ as in step 1. The natural contravariant mapping-space/colimit formula in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,q)$ with
$$\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(P(j),z)\ \longrightarrow\ \lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(P(j),Ry).$$
Every component is an equivalence by the preceding conclusion. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] this natural transformation of diagrams of spaces is an equivalence, and a limit functor carries an equivalence and its inverse to inverse equivalences. Hence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,q)$ is an equivalence for every $x$. All these limit diagrams have small index $J^{\mathrm{op}}$; no colimit or limit indexed by the possibly large category $\mathcal C$ is taken. Here the mapping-space/limit statement is used in containing universes large enough for the space category in the compactness definition; the index J is still small in the original universe.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7.7, proof: the generator-evaluation test, expanded using compact presentations and the mapping-space colimit formula (Proposition 5.1.3.2).

proof.text: Taking components in step 4 with $x=Ry$ gives an edge $v:Ry\to z$ with $[q][v]=1_{Ry}$. With $x=z$, injectivity of the same map on components and the equation $[q][v][q]=[q]$ give $[v][q]=1_z$. By the homotopy-category and equivalence criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], these two equations say that $q$ is an equivalence edge. Its coherent identification with the cocones in step 3 therefore identifies the image cocone $RT\to Ry$ with the chosen colimiting cocone $RT\to z$ by an equivalence of cocones. The cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] then makes $RT\to Ry$ colimiting: for every testing object, precomposition with the equivalence of vertices identifies its universal mapping-space map with that of $RT\to z$. Thus $R$ preserves the arbitrary small $\rho$-filtered colimit selected in step 3. The same $\rho$ was fixed in step 2 independently of $I$ and $T$, proving the statement.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7.7, proof: conclude preservation from the generator tests; comparison-map equivalence and the cocone conclusion written explicitly.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.4.7.7, proof (printed p. 451), read online: compact-generator and left-adjoint-image argument. The restricted-Yoneda detection step is expanded directly by presentations and mapping-space limits rather than invoking the entire theorem. The source is not archived in literature/.

Reused the existing common compactness rank and mapping-space/cone calculus nodes. The statement is unchanged.
